questions.prompt: Which volcanic forcing mechanisms explains why climate models that only reduce the solar constant tend to overestimate the cooling effect of volcanic eruptions?
questions.answer: They neglect longwave absorption and stratospheric heating by sulphate aerosol. Volcanic sulphate aerosol not only reflects solar radiation (causing a cooling effect) but also absorbs terrestrial and near-IR radiation, offsetting part of the cooling effect.
options: They neglect longwave absorption and stratospheric heating by sulphate aerosol.

questions.prompt: Two eruptions inject the same mass of SO\(_2\) into the atmosphere. Eruption A occurs in the tropical stratosphere, while Eruption B occurs at high latitude in the Northern Hemisphere. Which is most likely?
questions.answer: Eruption A produces a longer-lasting and more globally distributed aerosol cloud. This is because aerosol injected into the tropical stratosphere is transported more widely and remains in the atmosphere longer. An eruption at high latitude is more likely to be confined to the hemisphere of the eruption and to be removed more quickly by stratosphere-troposphere exchange.
options: Both produce identical global aerosol lifetimes.
Eruption B produces a longer-lasting global aerosol perturbation.
Eruption A produces a longer-lasting and more globally distributed aerosol cloud.
Latitude has little influence once SO₂ reaches the stratosphere.

questions.prompt: What is the value of π (pi)?
questions.answerInfo: Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, so it is dimensionless.

questions.prompt: What is the standard acceleration due to gravity at Earth's surface?
questions.answerInfo: This is the conventional standard gravity.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are greenhouse gases?
questions.answer: The greenhouse gases are carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor. Oxygen is not a greenhouse gas.
